findings.title: Write endpoints lack idempotency key support
findings.description: POST /orders, POST /orders/:id/refund, and POST /orders/:id/cancel have no idempotency key support. A duplicate call to refund double-refunds. SAFETY.md documents this as a deliberate gap.
findings.gap: No Idempotency-Key header support, no deduplication logic, no unique constraint enforcement on business keys for write operations.
findings.recommendation: Add Idempotency-Key header support to all state-mutating POST endpoints using middleware that stores keys in PostgreSQL or Redis.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no idempotency keys on write endpoints.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: API-Q4 fired because POST /orders/:id/refund issues real money movement with no Idempotency-Key — a duplicate call double-refunds. All three write POST endpoints lack deduplication.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add Idempotency-Key header support to POST /orders and POST /orders/:id/refund using a middleware.
blocker_remediation.target_state: All state-mutating POST endpoints accept and enforce an idempotency key. Duplicate requests with the same key return the original response.

findings.title: No immutable audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No audit logging of authenticated principal for write operations. DELETE /orders/:id performs irreversible hard delete with no audit record. Refund and cancel operations lack principal attribution in logs.
findings.gap: No per-operation audit trail recording authenticated principal, action, and affected resources. No immutable log storage.
findings.recommendation: Add structured audit log emission in each write route handler capturing principal (from JWT), action, resource ID, timestamp. Configure immutable log storage.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no audit logging exists for write operations.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: AUTH-Q6 fired because write handlers (delete, refund, cancel) execute without logging the authenticated principal. SAFETY.md confirms 'no audit trail' for destructive operations.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add structured audit log emission in each write handler.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every write operation logs the authenticated principal to an immutable audit trail.

findings.title: No compensation or rollback for multi-step operations
findings.description: Multi-step write operations have no compensation or rollback. The refund method updates order status AND calls payment processor — if payment fails, status is already changed. cancelAndRecallShipment updates status AND recalls dispatch. hardDelete permanently removes data.
findings.gap: No saga pattern, no compensating transactions, no undo endpoints, no soft-delete. Partial state corruption possible on multi-step failures.
findings.recommendation: Wrap multi-step operations in database transactions. Add soft-delete. Implement compensating logic for external call failures.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no rollback/compensation exists for multi-step write workflows.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: STATE-Q1 fired because refund and cancel operations perform database writes followed by external service calls with no transaction boundary or compensation on failure.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Wrap multi-step operations in database transactions with rollback on external call failure.
blocker_remediation.target_state: All multi-step operations are atomic or compensatable. Deleted records are soft-deleted.

findings.title: No data residency governance for customer PII
findings.description: Customer PII stored in PostgreSQL without documented residency requirements or technical controls to prevent cross-border transmission by an agent. Single-region deployment (infra/ecs.yaml) but no enforcement mechanism.
findings.gap: No documented data residency policy. No technical controls restricting data transmission across jurisdictions.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements. Classify data fields by sensitivity and residency constraints. Implement controls for agent-initiated data handling.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND customer PII stored without residency governance.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q2 fired because the service stores customer PII (labeled in SAFETY.md) without any data residency documentation or technical controls to prevent an agent from transmitting it cross-jurisdictionally.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Document data residency requirements for customer order data. Classify data fields.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Residency policy documented and enforced. API responses annotated with residency constraints.

findings.title: No identity propagation to downstream services
findings.description: JWT tokens validated at API boundary but no identity propagation to downstream WarehouseClient calls. No on-behalf-of flow or token exchange. Cannot distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.gap: No identity propagation to downstream services. No mechanism to distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.recommendation: Implement token exchange or pass-through of caller JWT claims to downstream service calls.

compensating_controls: Restrict agent to read-only until propagation implemented
Add caller identity to downstream headers manually

findings.title: No immediate agent identity suspension mechanism
findings.description: JWT-based auth relies on token expiry for revocation. No token deny-list or immediate suspension mechanism in the application.
findings.gap: No in-application token deny-list. Immediate revocation depends entirely on external IdP.
findings.recommendation: Add a token deny-list cache (Redis-backed) checked on each request, or implement jti claim validation against a revocation store.

compensating_controls: API Gateway-level deny-list for agent client IDs

findings.title: No concurrency controls on write operations
findings.description: No optimistic or pessimistic locking. Multiple concurrent agent instances could issue conflicting updates. No version fields, ETags, or SELECT FOR UPDATE patterns.
findings.gap: No concurrency controls. Race conditions possible on concurrent write operations.
findings.recommendation: Add version column and optimistic locking (WHERE version = $expected). Return ETag headers on GET.

compensating_controls: Limit to single agent instance per operation type
Database unique constraints on status transitions

findings.title: No circuit breakers for external dependency calls
findings.description: OrderService calls WarehouseClient (issueRefund, recallDispatch) with no circuit breaker, retry logic, or timeout. Failing warehouse causes cascading failures.
findings.gap: No circuit breaker pattern. No retry with backoff. No timeout on external calls.
findings.recommendation: Implement circuit breaker on WarehouseClient calls. Add configurable timeouts and exponential backoff.

compensating_controls: ALB/ECS health checks detect cascade failures
HTTP client timeout for warehouse calls

findings.title: No rate limiting on API endpoints
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. SAFETY.md documents: 'No rate limiting; an automated caller can fan out unchecked.' No API Gateway throttle in IaC, no application middleware.
findings.gap: No rate limits. Runaway agent loop can DDoS the service.
findings.recommendation: Add @fastify/rate-limit middleware with per-client limits. Configure ALB or API Gateway throttling.

compensating_controls: Per-client request quotas at API Gateway

findings.title: No business-level transaction limits
findings.description: No configurable transaction limits. No maximum refund amount per session, no maximum deletes per time window, no per-caller business operation caps.
findings.gap: No business-level transaction limits. Unlimited agent-initiated operations possible.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller transaction limits: max refund amount per hour, max deletes per session.

findings.title: No draft/pending state for write operations
findings.description: All write operations immediately committed. Order status enum (placed, shipped, cancelled, refunded) has no PENDING or DRAFT state. Agent-initiated refund or cancellation executes immediately.
findings.gap: No draft/pending state mechanism. All writes are final on execution.
findings.recommendation: Add PENDING states to order lifecycle. Separate mutation into proposal and confirmation steps.

findings.title: No configurable approval gates for high-risk operations
findings.description: No approval workflow for refunds, cancellations, or hard deletes. SAFETY.md identifies need for 'human approval above a threshold' and 'human-in-the-loop confirmation.'
findings.gap: No configurable approval gates. No operation-level flags to require human confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Implement threshold-based approval gates with approval request/grant flow.

findings.title: No PII redaction in application logs
findings.description: Service handles customer PII. README documents structured logging (pino) but no PII redaction mechanism visible. No log scrubbing middleware or masking library.
findings.gap: No PII redaction. Customer data may be logged unmasked.
findings.recommendation: Implement pino serializers that redact PII fields from log output.

compensating_controls: Pino serializers to redact sensitive fields

findings.title: Error responses lack retryable indicator
findings.description: Error responses use consistent {code, message} format but lack a retryable boolean or error category for agent self-correction.
findings.gap: No retryable boolean or error category in error responses.
findings.recommendation: Add retryable field to error response schema.

findings.title: No async pattern for external service calls
findings.description: Refund and cancel operations call external services synchronously. No background job framework or polling endpoints.
findings.gap: No async operation support for potentially long-running external calls.
findings.recommendation: Convert long-running operations to async with job submission and polling endpoint.

findings.title: No input validation at API boundary
findings.description: No input validation library used. Route handlers cast request bodies with TypeScript type assertions without runtime validation.
findings.gap: No systematic input validation. Malformed payloads accepted without structured rejection.
findings.recommendation: Add Fastify schema validation using built-in ajv support. Define request body schemas for write endpoints.

findings.title: No temporal metadata on order records
findings.description: Order interface has no created_at, updated_at, or event_time fields. No data freshness indicators in API responses.
findings.gap: No timestamp fields. Agents cannot determine data freshness.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at/updated_at columns and Last-Modified response headers.

findings.title: No breaking change detection for API contracts
findings.description: OpenAPI spec versioned (2.1.0) but no URL versioning, no CI-based breaking change detection, no contract tests.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings could break silently on API changes.
findings.recommendation: Add API version prefix to routes and integrate OpenAPI diff tooling into CI.

findings.title: No distributed tracing instrumentation
findings.description: Structured logging claimed (pino with request_id) and CloudWatch Logs configured, but no distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry/X-Ray). Cannot trace requests through downstream services.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing. Cannot debug agent-initiated requests across service boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK or AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing. Propagate traceparent header.

findings.title: No alerting configuration for API degradation
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms defined. No alerting for error rates, latency, or anomaly detection.
findings.gap: API degradation affecting agents would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for 5xx rate, p99 latency, and task health.

findings.title: IaC governance incomplete — no review or drift detection
findings.description: CloudFormation template exists (infra/ecs.yaml) but no CI/CD enforces peer review. No drift detection configured.
findings.gap: IaC exists but lacks change review enforcement and drift detection (1/3 sub-checks pass).
findings.recommendation: Add CI/CD with mandatory review for IaC changes. Enable AWS Config drift detection.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline with API contract testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration exists. No contract testing, no automated validation before production.
findings.gap: No CI/CD pipeline. API contract changes not caught before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with contract testing validating against openapi/orders.yaml.

findings.title: Zero automated test coverage
findings.description: Vitest configured in package.json but no test files exist. Zero automated test coverage for agent-facing APIs.
findings.gap: No test files despite framework being configured.
findings.recommendation: Write integration tests covering all endpoints: input validation, error responses, auth, and business logic.

findings.title: No encryption at rest configuration for data store
findings.description: RDS stores customer data but no encryption configuration visible in repository IaC. No StorageEncrypted or KMS key defined.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest configuration in this repository's IaC.
findings.recommendation: Define RDS with StorageEncrypted: true and customer-managed KMS key in IaC.

findings.title: No sandbox or staging environment for agent testing
findings.description: No separate environment configurations, no docker-compose, no seed data scripts.
findings.gap: No safe environment for testing agent behavior before production.
findings.recommendation: Add docker-compose.yml for local dev. Create environment-specific CloudFormation parameters.

findings.title: No formal data classification metadata
findings.description: System handles customer PII and financial data. API responses are appropriately scoped (order-domain fields only). Access differentiation exists (read/write roles). However, no formal classification tags or PII detection tooling.
findings.gap: No formal data classification metadata — aspirational gap only (B3).
findings.recommendation: Add data classification tags to IaC resources and field-level sensitivity annotations in OpenAPI spec.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Stage A: Yes (customer PII). Stage B: B1 CLEAR (responses scoped), B2 CLEAR (access differentiated), B3 INFO (no formal classification). Overall: INFO.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 B1 did not fire because API responses contain only order-domain fields (id, customerId, status, totalCents) — no password hashes or unnecessarily exposed sensitive fields. B2 did not fire because read/write role differentiation exists.

b1.reasoning: API responses return order-relevant fields only. No sensitive field leakage detected.

b2.reasoning: Role-based access (orders:read vs orders:write) provides access differentiation.

b3.reasoning: No formal data classification tags, PII detection tooling, or field-level sensitivity annotations.

findings.title: No event emission for state changes
findings.description: State changes (order creation, refund, cancellation) are not emitted as events. No SNS, EventBridge, or webhook integration.
findings.gap: Event-reactive agent patterns not supported. Must poll for state changes.
findings.recommendation: Emit events on state transitions to SNS or EventBridge.

findings.title: No rate limit documentation or headers
findings.description: No rate limits documented in OpenAPI spec. No X-RateLimit-Remaining or Retry-After headers in responses.
findings.gap: Agents cannot self-throttle based on rate limit feedback.
findings.recommendation: When rate limiting is implemented, add standard rate limit headers and document in OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: No data quality metrics or monitoring
findings.description: No data quality dashboards, profiling, null rate monitoring, or freshness SLAs for order data.
findings.gap: Agents cannot assess data reliability.
findings.recommendation: Define data quality SLAs and expose quality metrics.

findings.title: No data catalog or metadata layer
findings.description: No formal data catalog, metadata layer, or data dictionary. Schema inferred from SQL queries in code.
findings.gap: Agent tool developers must reverse-engineer data model from source.
findings.recommendation: Document data model formally or integrate with metadata service.

findings.title: No custom business outcome metrics
findings.description: No custom CloudWatch metrics for business events (order rate, refund rate, cancellation rate).
findings.gap: Cannot measure business outcomes of agent interactions.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom metrics for orders, refunds, cancellations.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: REST API documented via OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec (openapi/orders.yaml) and implemented via Fastify routes (src/routes.ts).

evaluations.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
evaluations.reason: OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec exists at openapi/orders.yaml with operation IDs and security scheme.

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: Responses are JSON (Fastify default serialization). Ideal format for LLM consumption.

evaluations.title: Machine Identity Authentication
evaluations.reason: JWT RS256 with JWKS validation, issuer/audience enforcement, and role claims provide machine identity authentication with principal attribution.

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
evaluations.reason: Role-based access differentiates orders:read from orders:write. Agent identities can be scoped to read-only.

evaluations.title: Action-Level Authorization
evaluations.reason: Action-level auth enforced: orders:read for GET, orders:write for mutations. Agent can read without write access.

evaluations.title: Credential Management
evaluations.reason: Credentials managed via AWS Secrets Manager (infra/ecs.yaml). No hardcoded secrets. JWKS/issuer from env vars.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: GET /orders/:id returns current order state with status field. Agents can read-before-write.

evaluations.title: Rollback Capability
evaluations.reason: ECS DeploymentCircuitBreaker with Rollback: true provides automatic rollback on failed deployments.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: Field names are clear and semantic: customerId, totalCents, status. No legacy abbreviations.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no P0 priority designation or critical path evidence.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no list/query endpoints with potentially unbounded results. Only single-resource GET by ID.

items.summary: Resolve all 4 BLOCKERs (idempotency, audit logging, compensation/rollback, data residency) and address critical RISK-SAFETY findings (rate limiting, concurrency, circuit breakers, HITL controls, PII redaction) to move toward Pilot-Ready.
Address remaining safety risks (identity propagation, transaction limits) and quality gaps (input validation, observability, CI/CD, encryption) to improve operational readiness.
Address remaining quality and informational items: test coverage, data classification, event emission, and catalog/metrics.

recommended_actions.action: Add idempotency keys to write endpoints
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents duplicate operations (double-refunds, duplicate orders) when agents retry on timeout.
Required for compliance and forensics. Every write must attribute the authenticated principal.
Multi-step operations leave partial state on failure. Soft-delete enables recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Document and enforce data residency policy
recommended_actions.rationale: Customer PII requires residency governance before agent-initiated cross-border transmission.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy rate limiting and transaction caps
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents runaway agent loops from overwhelming the service or causing unbounded business impact.
High-risk operations (refund, cancel, delete) need approval gates and pending states.
